answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a terrace as the anchor of the cost.
